messages:
Maya (Finance): Heads-up: small but important update to the emergency PO and high-value vendor escalation flow effective Mon Sep 7. Posting summary here; full doc and FAQ on Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/finance/emergency-po-update :loudspeaker:

Alex (Procurement): TL;DR:
- Emergency PO window tightened: requests must include a business-impact statement + manager approval.
- For charges > $30k, Procurement + Legal must be looped before payment, even if marked emergency.
- Temporary virtual-card issuance for emergencies now capped at $5k per card.

Jordan (Vendor Ops): Practical note: vendor onboarding for emergency payments still requires W-9/W-8 and bank info within 48h of payment; missing docs will trigger holdback of subsequent invoices.

Maya (Finance): Why the change: we saw a few large emergency payments slip through without legal review. This is to keep risk low while still allowing urgent buys. If teams expect >$30k emergency spend, start the rapid review flow (procurement ticket + "EXPEDITE") so Legal can triage.

Priya (Legal): Quick legal checklist: any emergency payment that includes new contract terms, refunds, or indemnity changes must get Legal approval before vendor signs. If impossible, document attempts to obtain review in the ticket and Legal will provide retro guidance.

Alex (Procurement): Emergency card requests: include project, expiration (max 7 days), and justification. Cards issued are single-use recommended. For repeat emergency spend on same vendor, we'll convert to PO and require post-hoc reconciliation.

procurement-bot: System note: new emergency_po_flow automated checks added. Tickets missing manager approval or business-impact justification will be auto-returned. (Ref: EMPO-2026-09) :gear:

Jordan (Vendor Ops): Ops ask: will AP still process emergency vendor invoices if bank details are pending? A few international vendors take longer to provide docs.
\nMaya (Finance): AP will process one-time emergency payment if Procurement flags the ticket with "EMERGENCY-PROCESSED" and vendor bank details are on file within 48h. For international vendors with delays, Procurement can issue v-card up to $5k; wires require bank info first.

Alex (Procurement): Action items: 1) Teams that regularly use emergency flows please schedule a 10-min sync with Procurement so we can precollect vendor docs. 2) If you need a walkthrough, reply here with availability.

Priya (Legal): We'll publish a short emergency checklist and a sample manager approval note you can paste into tickets.

Maya (Finance): Thanks all. We'll monitor for a month and adjust thresholds if needed. If you hit a blocker, open ticket subject: "PROCURE-EMERGENCY-ESCALATE" and tag @Alex. :white_check_mark:
